notes: No amp+cab block — running into tube amp. CONFIRMED STUDIO RIG from Sound on Sound production article: nearly all guitar parts recorded using Kapranos's battered old Selmer valve combo amp and Hardy's Fender Bassman 100. No amp+cab model available for Selmer on Helix — the Selmer is a vintage British valve amp with EL84 power tubes, similar in character to a Vox AC30. EQ compensates for removed amp voicing. CRITICAL SONG NOTE: Take Me Out has a famous and deliberate tempo change — the angular intro riff is at approximately 104 BPM, and the main driving section kicks in at 133 BPM. Master BPM set to 133 (dominant section). Intro snapshot delay is set as a fixed ms value (345ms) since no note division lands cleanly at 104 BPM. Main riff and lead snapshot delays are tempo-synced to 133 BPM. Three snapshots: angular intro, driving main riff, and lead/solo. Deranged Master (Dallas Rangemaster Treble Booster) approximates Kapranos's confirmed Telenordia Treble Booster for main riff. Elephant Man (EHX Deluxe Memory Man) chosen for delay — its modulation approximates the wobbly character of Kapranos's confirmed Gurus Echosex 2 (Binson Echorec-style).
confirmed_sources: Sound on Sound — Recording Franz Ferdinand (Selmer amp + Fender Bassman 100)
Equipboard — Alex Kapranos gear (Telenordia Treble Booster, Gurus Echosex 2, Fender Hot Rod Deluxe live 2004)

tempo_change_note: Take Me Out has a famous deliberate tempo change at approximately 0:53. The intro (Snapshot 1) is at ~104 BPM. The main section (Snapshots 2+3) is at ~133 BPM. Use tap tempo on the Helix to lock to each section. Master BPM is set to 133 for the main section — tap before Snapshot 1 to adjust intro delay if needed, or leave it as a fixed ms value.

noise_gate.notes: Intro snapshot most open — angular clean riff must decay naturally. Main riff tightens as Deranged Master adds noise. Lead snapshot tightens further.

treble_booster.notes: Confirmed: Kapranos uses a Telenordia Treble Booster on his 2022 live rig. Deranged Master (Dallas Rangemaster) is the closest available model — treble boosters were the original British tone-shaping pedal, cutting low end and boosting high-mid frequencies before a valve amp. WARNING from YAML: 'Like the real thing, this model can take your head off! Works best before a distorted amp.' BYPASSED in Snapshot 1 (angular intro — clean and angular, no boost needed). ACTIVE in Snapshots 2 and 3. Drive kept conservative — the Rangemaster into a valve amp should add presence and bite, not fuzz.

eq.notes: Compensates for removed Selmer valve amp voicing. The Selmer is a British EL84-powered amp with a bright, slightly spiky midrange character — similar to a Vox AC30 but more raw and unrefined. Mid boost at 800-900Hz adds the angular, percussive mid presence of the Selmer character. High Cut kept relatively open — the Selmer and Rangemaster combination has a naturally bright top end that should not be over-tamed. Intro snapshot uses a slightly different voicing — more open and jangly for the clean angular riff character.

delay.notes: Chosen over Cosmos Echo and Adriatic Delay specifically for the Mode and Depth parameters which approximate the Gurus Echosex 2 / Binson Echorec's characteristic wobble. Kapranos described the Echosex as having 'a bit of wobble in it as if like you've got a wonky wheel on the original.' Mode set to Chorus, Depth at low value adds subtle pitch modulation to repeats — this is the Echorec character. S1 intro: FIXED ms value of 345ms — no note division lands cleanly at 104 BPM within 20ms tolerance. S2 main riff: tempo-synced to 133 BPM, eighth note (225ms — near exact match 0.6ms off). S3 lead: tempo-synced to 133 BPM, dotted eighth (338ms — near exact match 0.3ms off).

reverb.notes: Room Size FIXED at 15m — do NOT make snapshot-variable, causes audible algorithm bump. The recording has a tight, slightly live room quality — not a large hall. Intro uses moderate reverb for the angular riff's space. Main riff is relatively dry and punchy — the driving rhythm section needs to cut through. Lead opens up for melodic passages.

1_angular_intro.description: Angular intro riff at ~104 BPM. Deranged Master bypassed — clean and angular, no treble boost. Gate open at -68dB. Moderate EQ — bright and jangly. Fixed 345ms delay (no division lands cleanly at 104 BPM) with Chorus modulation at Depth 15. Moderate reverb (1.5 sec, 28% mix). Switch to FS2 at the famous tempo change around 0:53.

2_main_riff.description: Main driving section at 133 BPM. Deranged Master active — treble boost into tube amp adds presence and bite. Tempo-synced eighth note delay (226ms, 22% mix). Dry, punchy reverb (0.7 sec, 12% mix). Tighter gate. The angular, percussive post-punk rhythm character.

3_lead.description: Lead passages and post-chorus sections. Deranged Master active with slightly higher Drive and Level. Tempo-synced dotted eighth delay (338ms, 38% mix) — more prominent for lead lines to bloom. Elephant Man Depth 18 — more wobble on lead repeats. More reverb (1.8 sec, 32% mix) for melodic passages to breathe.

playing_notes.tempo_change_technique: The shift from intro to main section at around 0:53 is one of the most recognizable moments in 2000s indie rock. It should feel like the song suddenly locks into a gear and accelerates. Switch from Snapshot 1 to Snapshot 2 exactly on the first downbeat of the main riff. The Deranged Master engaging simultaneously with the tempo change reinforces the dramatic shift.
playing_notes.pickup_notes: Bridge pickup throughout Snapshots 1 and 2 — the angular, cutting tone demands maximum attack and presence. Bridge or neck for Snapshot 3 depending on the specific lead passage.
playing_notes.deranged_master_note: The Deranged Master (Rangemaster treble booster) works best before a valve tube amp — its Bass at 3.0 rolls off the low end while Treble at 7.0 emphasizes the high-mid attack. This gives the main riff its characteristic percussive, slightly spiky quality that the Selmer valve amp and EL84 power tubes would naturally reinforce.
playing_notes.elephant_man_wobble: The Elephant Man's Depth parameter at 12-18 in Chorus mode adds a barely perceptible pitch fluctuation to the delay repeats — this is the Echorec character Kapranos described as the 'wonky wheel' wobble. At these low Depth values it should feel like an organic, slightly imperfect analog quality rather than an obvious modulation effect.
playing_notes.guitar_note: Kapranos used his battered old Selmer amp in the studio with presumably his guitars of the period — a Fender Telecaster Deluxe '72 style guitar is consistent with the bright, cutting attack of the recording. Your Strat Plus Deluxe's Lace Sensor bridge pickup will give a similar single-coil attack character. Use bridge pickup for all rhythm and main riff work.
